utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: How was this document drafted; can you tell us this?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When Nenad and Fuad agreed to what was going to be said, then I was dictated what they said.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: In the first document which is marked D26/1, in other words, the document which you said you drafted yourself, the heading says that this was an agreement between the representatives of the Croatian and Bosniak Muslim side at Nenad's place.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, this is how I understood it, and that is how I wrote it down.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: The second document which you drafted about two hours later, it is stated that this was an agreement between the Santici HVO and the representatives of the Bosniak Muslim side in Ahmici. The place and date are the same. Why was this change put in? Why was it now that the representatives of the Croatian side were replaced by the Santici HVO side? What was the change about?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know. It was just dictated to me this way. I don't know whether Nenad had anything to do with the local HVO government in Vitez, but I can only assume that this was so.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Did you sign this second document?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, as a third person, where it states "for the HVO."

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Was this document signed by the Muslims mentioned here and in your presence?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I remember Muris Ahmic with certainty, and as regards these three other documents, I cannot even recall that anybody else was present at that meeting. I cannot say with certainty, but I think that those people were not present at the meeting. Perhaps they signed it subsequently. Maybe it's not so, but I do not recall them being present there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: You also said that Fuad Berbic was present at the other meeting; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: How come he did not sign this record?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Fuad was upset with the situation, as it turned out. It was as if he predicted -- but I don't know what he meant. He was then relieved of his duty, and he was upset, and so he said, "You sign it because you are the commander."

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: The record states that it is requested of the Muslim population of Ahmici to turn over and surrender their weapons to the HVO in the interests of preserving peace in Santici and Ahmici. What was the reason for the surrender of weapons on the basis of what was being discussed?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This sentence was written down on the basis of the discussions which were conducted previously between Nenad and Fuad when it became clear that the Muslims were to blame for the conflict, that they were responsible for setting up the barricade, as Fuad had said, and then in order to ensure that this would not be repeated, this type of agreement was reached.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: The Muslims who were present at the meeting, primarily Muris Ahmic and Fuad Berbic, did they blame the Croats from the village for taking part in the conflict in the village? Did they lodge any complaints against the Croats in the village?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Fuad said that he knew that the soldiers from Busovaca and Kiseljak were responsible, but he said that no one among the Croats from the village had taken part in this conflict.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: In the next sentence, it is stated that Santici is guaranteeing the safety of Muslims in this area. Who was it? Who was involved in the Santici HVO at that time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Again, I wrote this as dictated. It was agreed between the two of them, and I don't know who was in the Santici HVO at that time. I don't know whether Nenad Santic had anything to do with it, being the representative of the civilian government there. I don't know if he had anything to do with it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: It is also stated further that a joint commission composed of the representatives of Muslim and Croat people would be established in order to prevent further conflicts, and it is also mentioned that the aggressors who are being mentioned, are specified, they are specified as being Chetniks.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At that time, the common enemy was the Serbs. They were the enemies of both the Croats and Muslims, and they were on Mount Vlasic and Turbe. I really liked the idea; however, it was never implemented.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Further on, it is stated that this unit was not going to be used in fighting against the Muslim people or the Croatian people in any areas, so it's not just limited to Ahmici and Santici?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. On that day, there was a conflict in Novi Travnik over some gas station between the Croats and Muslims, and my assumption was that this was going to be also applied to that situation, that it was going to cover all areas.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: It is also mentioned that on the basis of what was said, the return of refugees, both Muslim and Croatian, to their own homes is also going to be guaranteed. Can you say on that day, who were the Croatian refugees in Santici and Ahmici at that time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was us, the Kupreskic families, and Dragan Vidovic with his family. We were the only refugees.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So both sides admitted at that time that there were both Muslim and Croatian refugees in that area; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The only thing that I was directly involved in, by my own account, was this because I was at that time away from my house with my family and my brother's family, so I insisted that this be put in there because I was not able to be in my house on those days.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: It is also mentioned here that both sides would guarantee a peaceful coexistence between the Muslims and the Croats.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Did you believe in such guarantees and did you believe in the possibility of peaceful coexistence?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I absolutely believed in the possibility of peaceful coexistence, as I believe that it is going to be possible in the future, but whether anything else was going to be realised, I did not know. I thought that Nenad and Fuad were going to transmit all this to someone in Vitez and that something would be done about it, but I learned that nothing was accomplished, except that the refugees were able to return to their homes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So this joint unit of Croatian and Muslim people was never established?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Do you know whether, on the basis of this agreement, weapons were taken away from the Muslim population in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At that time, I do not know that any weapons were taken away from anyone, and in the subsequent days, I learned, I believe it was from my brother, that Fahran told him, that the late Fahran said that he had turned in his weapon and some other people who lived alongside the road. I don't know how exactly these people were, but I did not hear that anybody had turned -- that people in the middle of Ahmici, the Upper Ahmici people who lived around the mosque area, I'm not aware of any one of those people having ever turned in their weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Did you do anything, take any action, in terms of trying to take any weapons from any of the Muslims after this?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Do you know whether any steps were taken against people who returned to the village and had not turned in their weapons?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No steps were taken, nor did anyone have any problems based on the fact that even though it was said that they should turn in their weapons, they did not, or at least I'm not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Regarding the persons who were known to have taken part in this conflict from the Muslim side, did they have any problems when they returned?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I do not know whether they had any problems. I know that Zahid Ahmic, who was with the military police and who lived down near the road, he was afraid for a while to come back, but after awhile, he also came back, and he had no problems, because the word got around that he was at the barricade, that he had taken some four rifles from the soldiers who were supposed to pass through there. I don't know if he had received any threats, but eventually, after 15 or 20 days, he came back.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Can you say, after 22 October, 1992, did you see any Muslims in the village carrying weapons?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I did, immediately afterwards. The first checkpoint at the entrance to the village was a joint one, and both sides had weapons. We also had joint guards, and there were even more weapons at the time. As I said, you could purchase some weapons, and there was an influx of refugees from Western Bosnia to Ahmici and in all of Central Bosnia, including Ahmici, so all this sort of settled down, and people went about their lives in, more or less, a normal way.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Can you recall perhaps when this checkpoint was placed at the entrance to Ahmici, what date that was, or, rather, approximately how many days after this?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I cannot recall exactly, but perhaps four or five days later, I returned home with my family, and a few days afterwards, the checkpoint was placed, perhaps two or three days after I returned home, that is to say, a total of seven, eight, or ten days. I can't say exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: This checkpoint was placed during the day, wasn't it, during daytime; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, for a certain time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: The Muslim and the Croat guards at that checkpoint came there armed; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Can you recall whether, in addition to these men at the checkpoint who came with weapons and the Muslim patrols that you also encountered in the village, and you saw that they were armed too, did you see any larger group of Muslim soldiers with weapons at that time in the area of Ahmici, of course?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: After the conflict, for a few days, there were no special movements. People were waiting to see what this would be like. However, as the situation calmed down, the Muslims rallied together in the school. They had weapons too, and a bus came. They established a unit, and then buses came that took them to Cekrcici, to the front line against the Serbs, so this was quite normal.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Do you remember any situation when you perhaps saw soldiers who went for reviews to Preocica, Vrhovine, and the other neighbouring villages?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I had the opportunity of seeing their departure by my house towards Barin Gaj and Vrhovine. How far they went, I don't know, but I was sitting at the balcony, and my estimate was that 50, up to 70 men passed by, partly wearing uniforms, partly armed, partly they did have uniforms, partly they did not. I cannot recall, but I think that Fuad was with them, and usually they would have a review, and then they would come back. This was the summer before the conflict, and after the conflict, I did not see this, but rumour had it that they did something similar, but they didn't go by our house. They didn't go by my house. They went in the other area, in Gornji Ahmici. I didn't see this, but I heard about it. Perhaps this was a month or two after the conflict.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: At the point when you wrote this agreement, could you have assumed what would happen in Ahmici within six months' time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: How could I? There was not a single indicator showing that something like that would happen. I could not have imagined anything like it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. President. I have concluded. If necessary, I can give further clarifications or explanations in relation to this document marked as D26/1. Indeed, we got it from the wife of Nenad Santic, and we don't have the original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: It now becomes D27/1, so it is a Defence Exhibit. Any objection from the Prosecution about this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: So they are all admitted into evidence. I think when this was first produced by the Prosecution, we could not verify whether or not the signature, the third signature on the left-hand side, was that of Zoran Kupreskic. Since now he has asserted that this is his signature, I think we can admit it into evidence. We can now move to the Prosecution because I assume there is no other Defence counsel prepared to cross-examine Mr. Zoran Kupreskic. This was my assumption. Maybe not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Your assumption was right, Mr. President. No other Defence attorneys are going to question the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Terrier?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Before beginning and in accordance with the ruling of the Trial Chamber, I should request permission to refer to four series of written documents, but in order to be able to freely mention the documents I am referring to, we need to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Mr. Zoran Kupreskic, you said a moment ago, this very morning, that what happened on the 16th of April, 1993 in Ahmici was a horrible crime, atrocious. This will perhaps facilitate many things. As we continue with the cross-examination and this trial, I should like you to be more precise in this connection, and I'm asking you whether today, during this testimony, you admit that the 16th of April, 1993, in Ahmici, a large number, a very large number of Muslim civilians, more than 100 Muslim civilians, including women and children, were murdered; do you admit that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I have nothing to admit or not admit in that regard. Everybody knows what happened in Ahmici, but the information about that was received in different ways, in five, seven, ten days, and as to the exact proportions of the crime, I only learned about it here at the Tribunal. I see it as a terrible crime, and I said that my conscience will be laid to rest only when the true perpetrators of this crime are brought to justice, but I do not know what I am doing here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, let us be quite clear. For the moment, I'm not asking you about your personal responsibility or about any links that may attach you to that crime, that is not my intention, but in a trial, one first has to establish the facts of the crime before examining the responsibilities for that crime, and I am talking about this first stage which I should like to focus on for a few minutes. In view of the fact of the charges made against you, it is important to know whether you admit that, in fact, a crime was committed today, in view of all that you knew before coming to The Hague and what you learnt after coming to The Hague. I'm also asking you whether you admit that several Muslim inhabitants of Ahmici were arrested and detained for several days in the school in Dubravica.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I have heard of it, but I did not see any of that, that is, regarding the school in Dubravica. I only heard about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Are you contesting the fact that virtually all the buildings and Muslim property in Ahmici was destroyed on the 16th of April and the next day?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I am not denying that fact, but I don't know whether almost all of the houses and properties were destroyed. In fact, some were not.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Do you admit that the two mosques in Ahmici, as well as the school, were destroyed on the 16th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Do you admit that what has been referred to, that is, the murders and the destruction, that they were the results of an attack by the armed forces of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I can only tie this -- but I do not have the real proof of it. If I did, I would gladly share it here. The only thing I can say is that the soldiers whom I saw that day and on three subsequent days, I have, in my mind, tied to this event, but I cannot say specifically who actually committed any of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Do you admit today that the attack against Ahmici was against a civilian population which was unable to defend itself, that the 16th of April, 1993 in Ahmici, there was no conflict between opposing armed forces, and that in Ahmici, there was no legitimate military target?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is several questions rolled into one, but I cannot admit to that or deny it because as I experienced the morning of the 16th, and I'm talking about the early morning, for me, it was like war. There was shooting going on on both sides, and the closest I came to an understanding of it was in the evening of the 16th, because around the mosque by the school, there was real fighting going on because shooting was coming from both sides, and then the next morning, it was coming on both sides. So I assumed, and I think I was aware that there were soldiers in the village, and so I cannot confirm what you have just said.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: When you're talking about a conflict on the 16th of April, 1993 in Ahmici, would you, nevertheless, admit today that not a single [Realtime transcript read in error "Muslim"] civilian living in Ahmici, Pirici, or Santici was killed or wounded on the 16th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know if any Croatian civilians were killed there. In other words, I am not aware of that fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Excuse me. There's an error in the transcript. You spoke about Croats, Croatian civilians, not Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: We need to correct the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Again, talking about the combat, would you admit, Mr. Witness, that on the 16th of April, 1993, not a single Croatian civilian was arrested and detained?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I have not heard of any such case either.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Do you admit that no Croatian property in Ahmici, Santici, or Pirici was destroyed or looted on the 16th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I cannot say so because I do not know, but there were some damaged houses on the Croatian side as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Do you recognise that no religious Catholic symbol was attacked on that day?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Radovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, we asked the witness at some point whether there was any Catholic places of worship there, and he said that there wasn't any, so how can a Christian place of worship have been damaged if it didn't exist? So I think that the whole question is misplaced.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: No, but Mr. Radovic, I don't agree with you. Allow me to disagree. Because there are not just churches, there could be crosses, cemeteries that were Catholic, as far as I know. So the crosses, the tombs, could be destroyed. So I think the question is absolutely relevant.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Could you please answer the question, Witness?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: There is no need for it to be repeated. I am aware of the cemetery in Topola, near the road, but whether it was damaged on that day, I do not know. But I also do not know of any other religious structure in that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Could you be more specific on this occasion, because I don't think it was ever mentioned what damage was inflicted on that day to the Catholic cemetery?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did not say that any damage was inflicted, I said that I was not aware that any damage had been done there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Very well. Finally, Mr. Witness, do you admit that Ahmici, Santici, and Pirici, which were mixed villages until the 16th of April, 1993, became, as of that day, a village that was 100 per cent Croat and that 500 or 600 Muslim inhabitants who had resided there before were forced to leave?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No Muslims stayed, as far as I know, following the 16th. For several days, there were some there, and some of them left of their own free will, certainly fearing the future and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: You said that some Muslims left Ahmici after the 16th of April of their own free will. Could you be more precise and give us some names or simply tell us where they lived?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When I said this, I had in mind Ramo Bilic and his family, the two Strmonja brothers, Miralen and Nermin, who had taken shelter alongside the Croats in Vinko Vidovic's house, and as Niko Santic told us later, they, of their own free will, left for fear of what was going to happen to them, and they're still alive today. I'm not sure, but they may have come back.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Would you know, please try and tell us, at what point in time you became aware of the crimes that have been described and of which you yourself admitted were horrible crimes? Did this awareness come to you gradually, did this awareness develop before you were brought to The Hague, or was it only in the course of this trial? Could you explain that to us?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I can say that I was learning about this crime step by step. If we talk about the first day, 16th of April, I had little information, and also people who were with me in the depression also knew very little. In the first hour, we only thought about the combat that was going on, and there were bullets flying through the trees and we could hear them in branches and they were coming from the other side. As the situation developed on that day and subsequent days, we learned that houses were burned down, that there were casualties. The first few days -- in fact, the first three days before we went up to Pirici, I did not see any burnt Croatian houses, only Muslim, but I learned of the deaths of both Muslims but also Mirjan Santic; and on the 18th, the key event which stays in my mind and which made me believe that crimes were committed was when I saw the body of Enver and when I saw some other bodies there, and the full extent of it, I learned, in fact, here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: When you refer to Enver, you are referring to Enver Sehic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It is Sehic, my next-door neighbour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: I apologise for mispronouncing the name. I should now like, Witness, for us to go back very briefly to your biography. You told us that you did your military service within the framework of the national army of the former Yugoslavia and that your specialisation was anti-chemical and nuclear warfare. In the course of your military service, did you have any special training also?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When I went to do my military service --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: I apologise. It was not correctly translated, what you just said. Could you repeat your last question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Yes, gladly, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: My question was as follows: During your military service, did you have any training in direct combat, foot soldier training?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Could you explain the term you used?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: What I mean by that term, Mr. President, a ground soldier, a foot soldier who is deployed on the ground, who is not in the air force or a sailor, an infantry soldier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: A foot soldier. Voila.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: All my training in the JNA was the same kind of training which is basic infantry training like any other soldier but since I also was in the school for reserve officers, I was on practice, and my speciality was the nuclear, biological, and chemical weapons. But for the most part, it was -- we were called dusters, as it was called. It was protection from nuclear and biological and chemical weapons, and in the class, we also covered those types of warfare.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Yes. But as a result, you also received training using rifles, automatic rifles, like the AK47?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Of course. As I said, every single soldier went through this training in using small arms weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: You told us in the course of your testimony that you acquired a rank, an officer's rank, in the army. Could you tell us when and what rank it was?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Every person, when they left the JNA and had trained as a reserve officer, I think that he is given a rank which is either a sergeant first class or staff sergeant. This is what you get sometimes at the time when you are released and sometimes when you report back into the defence department office.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: You personally, could you tell us the rank that you acquired at the end of your military service?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. It was either sergeant first class or staff sergeant. It was a sergeant of sorts, I only know that. I forget now.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Do you remember the year? What year was that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I served in the JNA from 1982 to 1983, eleven months.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Did you make any progress in rank either within the JNA, such as it existed, or within the framework of other units since then? I am talking up to April 1993, not what happened after that.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: During the first military exercise in which I took part, and it was the only one after I left the JNA, I received the rank of second lieutenant, and it was an automatic practice. Whoever had finished the school for reserve officers was accorded this rank automatically afterwards, and so was I.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. President, do you wish to adjourn now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: We will adjourn now until Monday at 9.00. Next week, we will be sitting from 9.00 to 1.00, every day from 9.00 to 1.00. All right? We stand adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: 1.00 p.m., to be reconvened on Monday, the 19th day of July, 1999, at 9.00 a.m. 24 25
